Republican leaders to take up a $350 billion defense spending package,
and Paris Claudia Grisales reports Senate Majority Leader John Thune says Republicans
are weighing their options.
President Trump posted on his social media account that Republicans can advance a partisan
military funding plan before Democrats take control of Congress next year.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune told NPR that remains to be seen.
"Everybody saw that, took note of it, and we're proceeding in a way to find out whether
or not that's a realistic option."
After losing big in the midterm elections, congressional Republicans said they're focused
on maximizing their legislative efforts in the lame duck session.
This week, Senate Republicans approved a conference resolution to "do everything humanly possible
to pass a partisan spending plan using an expedited process known as reconciliation."
Claudia Grisales, NPR News, The Capitol.
ICE says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any
time in its 23-year history.
ICE said that it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended September 30th,
up 9 percent from its previous high in the same period a year earlier.
ICE had not released such precise counts since President Trump returned to the White House,
including for 2025.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says there are new speed restrictions affecting
Star Shield, the military version of the Starlink satellite service the Ukrainian military uses
on the front lines, NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Zelensky warned the restrictions are helping Russia carry out more accurate attacks and
causing further Ukrainian casualties.
He said the restrictions have affected Ukrainian military operations for several days across
the entire front line and that the speed restrictions that kick in at 100 miles an hour make it
more difficult to intercept Russia's new jet-powered drones.
Zelensky said the speed restrictions are not due to random technical errors but are systematic.
They come just as the U.S. is again pushing negotiations to try to end the war.
Star Shield was first restricted three weeks ago as President Trump announced a diesel deal
with Russia.
Then it was reinstated, owner Elon Musk admitted he was behind slowing Starlink previously
but claimed the U.S. government controls access to Star Shield.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pir News, Kyiv.
Gaza's health ministry says an Israeli airstrike hit one of the main hospitals still operating
in the Gaza Strip today, killing six people including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy.
The Israeli military said the strike was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants without
providing evidence.
The commander it identified was not among the dead, the ministry and witnesses said the
strike hit the hospital's surgical wing.
The U.S. stock market fell today, the S&P 500 in Dowell fell more than a quarter percent.
This is NPR News.
The American Cancer Society is recommending routine prostate cancer screening for more
middle-aged men in a major change to its guidelines.
That means a blood test for what's called PSA or Prostate Specific Antigen.
The new guideline says men at average risk of getting prostate cancer should get a PSA
test every two years between the ages of 50 and 69.
Early childhood education builds a foundation for academic and other successes in life,
but as NPR's Janaki Mehta reports, the federal government found that in some states most
kids are not prepared for kindergarten.
Kindergarten is the entryway to public school, but not all kids enter with the skills they
need to succeed, including social and emotional development, language acquisition and motor
skills.
The Government Accountability Office and Independent Watchdog looked at data from Connecticut, Florida,
Kentucky, Maryland and Ohio to see how prepared its youngest were for kindergarten.
It found that fewer than half of students in all those states were ready.
White, Asian or students in lower poverty areas had better odds of being prepared, and
districts with more children who had been to preschool were also more likely to have
students that came in ready for kindergarten.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
A lightsaber used by Darth Vader in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi sold for
nearly $5 million in an auction today.
According to Heritage auctions, the sale marks a world auction record for any Star Wars collectible.
In July, Luke Skywalker's lightsaber and severed hand prop from Empire Strikes Back sold for
$3.75 million.
This is NPR News from Washington.
